Created comprehensive pytest suite (32 tests) covering uploads, CSV import, promotions, quicklinks, feature toggles, settings, pro registrations, forgot/reset password, audit log, analytics, soft-delete/restore/featured products, and seed data. 31/32 backend tests pass (96.9%). critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error when 'images' field is omitted or null in payload. ProductCreate declares images as Optional[List]=None which dumps to None, but Product model requires List (default []). Frontend ProductForm may not always send 'images: []'.
critical.fix: In create_product: pass `images = product.images or []` and `pdf = product.pdf` explicitly, or change Product.images validator to accept None and coerce to [].

critical.issue: 500 AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get' when product has no PDF. Line 488: `existing.get('pdf', {}).get('url')` fails because stored value is None, not missing.
critical.fix: Replace with `(existing.get('pdf') or {}).get('url')`. Same defensive pattern likely needed elsewhere if 'pdf' can be None.

minor.issue: Returns 403 instead of 401 (FastAPI HTTPBearer default behavior). Functionally correct but spec asked for 401. Cosmetic.

ui_bugs.issue: Logo image appears broken on homepage (broken-image icon top-left). settings.logo_url may point to a no-longer-existing file or default null with no fallback img element styling.

rca_of_the_issue: Bug 1 (POST /products 500): ProductCreate.images has type `Optional[List[ProductImage]] = None`. Calling Product(**product.model_dump()) feeds images=None into Product where images is `List[ProductImage] = []` — Pydantic v2 rejects None for list_type. Fix: use exclude_none=True in model_dump() or set images: List[ProductImage] = [] in ProductCreate too. Bug 2 (permanent-delete 500): when product was created without a PDF, MongoDB stores pdf: None (because POST inserts it as None via the model). Then `existing.get('pdf', {})` returns None (key exists), not {}, so `.get('url')` raises AttributeError. Fix: `(existing.get('pdf') or {}).get('url')`.
